qa1e298b8.question: ts1 (partial): no Epic acceptance criteria exist for this standalone bugfix; ac1-ac5 are LLD-local and trace to SPEC-34d7bb72 decisions 1-5.
qa1e298b8.rationale: Standalone bugfix: the approved SPEC-34d7bb72 is the source of truth; ac1-ac5 trace to its decisions 1-5. Consistent with the companion-template plan's resolution.

summary.prose: A standalone feature's LLD becomes the identity anchor of its work item, the same role a DEF plays for an Epic and an ISSUE plays for a fix, so the build tool can admit its plan's tasks one at a time. One reader in storage.ts decides what heads a work item (DEF, then ISSUE, then the story's LLD), and both the task resolver and folder naming use it, so they can no longer disagree. Head artifacts are named from a short written title instead of the first words of their prompt, everything downstream inherits that name, triage carries the SPEC a feature came from, and the existing docs migrator gathers already-split folders into one.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Anchor standalone features on their LLD so their plans build task by task

api.name: readEpicDefinitionCore
api.signature: readEpicDefinitionCore(repoPath: string, epicHash: string): EpicDefinitionCore  // EpicDefinitionCore gains readonly headKind?: 'DEF' | 'ISSUE' | 'LLD' and readonly tracker?: TrackerBlock

returns.meaning: The work item's head core (createdAt, epicSlug, standalone, tracker) from DEF-<h>, else ISSUE-<h>, else the lowest-ordinal LLD-<h>-<story> (any LLD, flagged standalone or not); headKind names which one answered; {} when none exists. An LLD head always reports standalone: true (a work item headed by an LLD has no DEF, so it is never an epic), and its createdAt is the LLD's epicCreatedAt when stamped, else its createdAt.

preconditions: Artifacts are read through readArtifactCore; a malformed file reads as empty and the next candidate is tried.
postconditions: DEF and ISSUE keep precedence over an LLD, so epic and bugfix work items resolve exactly as before.
readArtifactCore additionally reads meta.tracker, so readEpicIdentity keeps the tracker block (issue refs) it returns today for DEF/ISSUE epics.
An LLD head reports standalone: true even when the LLD itself carries no flag (legacy items), so every placement consumer files the item under docs/standalone.

api.name: readEpicIdentity
api.signature: readEpicIdentity(dir: string, epicHash: string): EpicIdentity | null

returns.meaning: {epicSlug, createdAt, tracker?} taken from the same head readEpicDefinitionCore selects (DEF, ISSUE, then LLD); null only when no head exists or it lacks epicSlug/createdAt.

postconditions: The DEF -> ISSUE -> LLD head order lives only in readEpicDefinitionCore; readEpicIdentity maps its result to {epicSlug, createdAt, tracker?} unchanged in shape.

resolve.ts readEpicDefinition (:209) deliberately stays DEF/ISSUE-only: it reads story DECLARATIONS for storyEvidence's 'declared' tier, and an LLD head's story existence is already proven by the 'artifact' tier (storyEvidence, resolve.ts:281), so an LLD needs no declaration path.

api.name: listEpicHashes

returns.meaning: DEF hashes, then ISSUE hashes, then hashes that have an LLD-<h>-<story> file and no DEF/ISSUE; each listed once, existing order unchanged.

postconditions: resolveByHier and an epicHash-scoped resolveByLabel now reach LLD-anchored work items, so resolveTaskRef admits their plan tasks from both build phases.

Unscoped resolveByLabel (resolve.ts:487-499) ranks LLD-headed hashes in a NEW lowest tier, consulted only when neither the explicit tier nor the implied tier yields a candidate. Whenever any DEF- or ISSUE-anchored work item evidences the label, the result is exactly today's (same winner, same ambiguity refusal); two LLD-headed candidates in that last tier refuse as ambiguous.

api.name: inheritedEpicSlug
api.signature: inheritedEpicSlug(repoPath: string, epicHash: string, fallback: string): string

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.purpose: Label used only when the work item has no head with a slug.

returns.meaning: The head's epicSlug (now including an LLD head), else fallback.

postconditions: finalizePlan and the BUILD/CR/TESTS writers land in the anchor LLD's folder for a standalone feature.

api.name: safeDeriveSlug
api.signature: safeDeriveSlug(focus: string | undefined): string  // unchanged; head finalizers now pass a title first

parameters.name: focus
parameters.purpose: Text to derive a label from; head finalizers pass their title when present, else their focus.

postconditions: finalizeBrainstorm labels from body.title, finalizeIssue from body.title, finalizeDefine from body.title, finalizeStandaloneLld (when no head exists yet) from params.storyTitle; each falls back to its focus when the title is absent.

api.name: planMigration

returns.meaning: Pure dry-run plan of moves; for a work item with no DEF/ISSUE, the label and anchor now come from its LLD before any other member.

postconditions: Label precedence is DEF -> ISSUE -> LLD -> other slug-carrying members -> flat filename -> hash.

workItemKind for a group with no DEF and no ISSUE member but an LLD member is 'standalone' (today it is 'standalone' only when some member carries the flag, migrate-docs-tree.ts:359), so legacy unflagged items consolidate under docs/standalone.
A dry run lists the consolidation moves for split standalone items without touching disk; applyMigration performs them.

dataModelChanges.details: Adds optional headKind ('DEF' | 'ISSUE' | 'LLD') and tracker (the meta.tracker block, now read by readArtifactCore so readEpicIdentity can delegate without losing issue refs). An LLD head is reported with standalone: true and createdAt = epicCreatedAt ?? createdAt.

Adds optional title (short, outcome-phrased) written by the brainstorm synthesizer in the same pass; the synthesizer schema asks for it; finalizeBrainstorm labels the SPEC folder from it. Existing SPECs without a title keep their focus-derived label.
Adds optional title written by the define synthesizer; finalizeDefine labels the Epic folder from it, falling back to focus.

insrc_triage start input gains optional specHash. phases/start.ts verifies it with requireApprovedSpec (existing, gates.ts:439; read-only use) before creating state; the TriageState type and state.ts encode/decode carry it (decodeState today rebuilds only runId/focus/repo, state.ts:32); classify's buildNextCall gains the specHash argument and forwards it into the design.story params (and the define params for an epic); the insrc_triage input schema registered in src/mcp/server.ts gains the optional field. No markdown change is needed: the LLD renderer already prints '**Seeded from:** SPEC-<hash>' when meta.seededFromSpec is set (src/workflow/artifacts/lld.ts:339-340), and finalizeStandaloneLld already stamps it (orchestrator.ts:2320, :2354); the gap is only that triage never passes specHash.

dataModelChanges.entity: readEpicDefinitionCore consumers (behaviour under an LLD head)
dataModelChanges.details: Every consumer and its behaviour once an LLD can head a work item: inheritedEpicSlug (storage.ts:223) -> the LLD's slug, so PLAN/BUILD/CR/TESTS share its folder; inheritedStandalone (storage.ts:240) and inheritedStoryStandalone (storage.ts:262) -> true, because an LLD head reports standalone: true; readEpicCreatedAt (storage.ts:273) -> the LLD's epicCreatedAt ?? createdAt, the same anchor buildRecordFolderArgs already uses for a standalone BUILD (callers: orchestrator.ts:1355/1817/2174 are DEF-headed and unchanged; orchestrator.ts:2331/2601/2611, tracker-auto.ts:147/220, tracker/link.ts:37 now get the LLD anchor instead of 'now'); buildRecordFolderArgs (storage.ts:383-416) -> unchanged result for flagged standalone items, and legacy unflagged items now resolve to the same LLD-derived folder; validate.ts resolveRouteFlag (src/mcp/build-step/phases/validate.ts:292-294) -> noHead becomes false for an LLD-only item, but the head now reports standalone: true, so inheritedStoryStandalone still returns true and BUILD/TESTS stay under docs/standalone (the ISSUE-0855311b placement invariant); completion-record.ts:58 and standalone-record.ts:267 (inheritedStoryStandalone) -> true for LLD-headed items; delivery graph placement (src/workflow/delivery/graph.ts:276, follows inheritedStoryStandalone) -> legacy unflagged items now show as standalone.

resolveByLabel's unscoped candidate tiers become explicit (DEF/ISSUE epics with an LLD/PLAN or a declared story) -> implied (ISSUE convention) -> LLD-headed (no DEF/ISSUE). The new tier is evaluated last, so a repo containing any DEF or ISSUE epic that evidences the label resolves exactly as today. Scoped (epicHash) and hierarchical resolution reach LLD-headed items directly.

errorCases.scenario: insrc_triage is started with a specHash whose SPEC is missing or not approved.
errorCases.detection: requireApprovedSpec throws SpecArtifactNotFoundError / SpecNotApprovedError at triage start.
errorCases.response: Triage start returns an error naming the spec and the reason; no state is created, so no nextCall can carry an unapproved spec.
errorCases.userImpact: The user approves the SPEC (or drops the specHash) and starts triage again.

errorCases.scenario: An LLD-anchored work item's LLD JSON is malformed or lacks createdAt/epicSlug.
errorCases.detection: readArtifactCore yields an empty core for the LLD, so readEpicDefinitionCore returns {} and readEpicIdentity returns null.
errorCases.response: The resolver treats the hash as unresolvable (same as today) and resolveTaskRef reports unresolved-target; slug inheritance uses its fallback.
errorCases.userImpact: Same failure as before the fix for that one item; others resolve.

errorCases.scenario: A head finalizer's synthesized title is present but produces a too-short slug (e.g. all stopwords).
errorCases.detection: deriveSlug throws on a slug shorter than MIN_LENGTH; safeDeriveSlug catches it.
errorCases.response: The finalizer falls back to its focus-derived label (safeDeriveSlug(focus)).
errorCases.userImpact: Folder named from focus, as today.

errorCases.scenario: planMigration finds a label or destination collision while consolidating a split standalone item.
errorCases.detection: The existing toSeen collision map and unmappable list in planMigration.
errorCases.response: The item is reported as unmappable with its reason and its files stay where they are; applyMigration refuses to run while unmappable entries exist, as today.
errorCases.userImpact: The dry run names the item to fix by hand.

edgeCases.expected: The ISSUE heads it (headKind 'ISSUE'); behaviour identical to today.

edgeCases.input: A standalone hash with LLDs for several stories (S001, S002).
edgeCases.expected: The lowest-ordinal LLD heads the work item, so every story shares one label and anchor date.

edgeCases.input: A legacy LLD without meta.standalone and without DEF/ISSUE.
edgeCases.expected: It heads its work item and is reported standalone: true; its plan tasks resolve; its BUILD/TESTS/CR are placed under docs/standalone; the migrator groups it as a standalone item.

edgeCases.input: A SPEC or DEF synthesized before this change (no title).
edgeCases.expected: Its existing focus-derived epicSlug is kept; nothing is renamed.

edgeCases.input: A standalone design.story started by hand without storyTitle.
edgeCases.expected: The LLD is labelled from its focus, as today; PLAN/BUILD/CR inherit that label.

edgeCases.input: A trivial or small standalone build (no PLAN).
edgeCases.expected: Unchanged: still built through the standalone build route without task resolution.

edgeCases.input: Unscoped 's1/t1' in a repo holding a DEF epic with s1 artifacts, an ISSUE bugfix and a standalone LLD+PLAN.
edgeCases.expected: Same result as today (the DEF epic's explicit evidence wins); the standalone item is only reachable unscoped when no DEF/ISSUE epic evidences s1, and is always reachable with its epicHash or hierarchical id.

migration.stateBefore: Per s1: the resolver (resolve.ts listEpicHashes/readEpicIdentity) and the slug inheritor (storage.ts readEpicDefinitionCore) each anchor a work item only on DEF or ISSUE, so standalone feature plans are unresolvable and their stages fall back to focus-derived labels; head finalizers label from the first words of focus; triage has no specHash input; planMigration labels an anchorless item from its first slug-carrying member by sorted id.
migration.stateAfter: One head reader (DEF -> ISSUE -> lowest-ordinal LLD) serves the resolver and slug inheritance; standalone plans build task by task; heads are labelled from a written title with focus fallback and downstream stages inherit; triage verifies and forwards an approved specHash; planMigration labels anchorless items from their LLD, and existing split standalone folders are consolidated.

migrationSteps.action: Make readEpicDefinitionCore the single head reader: add the LLD fallback, headKind and the tracker field (read by readArtifactCore), report an LLD head as standalone: true; have readEpicIdentity and listEpicHashes use it. Add the LLD-headed tier last in resolveByLabel's unscoped tiering.
Add optional title to SPEC and DEF bodies and their synthesizer schemas; label SPEC/DEF/ISSUE heads from their title and the standalone LLD from params.storyTitle, keeping the focus fallback.

Add optional specHash to the triage start input (types.ts, the server.ts schema), verify it in phases/start.ts with requireApprovedSpec, carry it through state.ts encode/decode, and forward it from classify into the design.story (and define) nextCall. The LLD's 'Seeded from' line already renders (artifacts/lld.ts:339); no change there.
In planMigration give the LLD label precedence after DEF and ISSUE, and group a work item with an LLD and no DEF/ISSUE as standalone.

Run planMigration as a dry run over this repo, review the listed consolidation moves for anchorless standalone items, then run applyMigration to move their md files into the anchor LLD's folder (git mv, one commit per work item).

migration.backwardCompat: All changes are additive or internal. DEF and ISSUE keep precedence, so epic and bugfix work items resolve and land exactly as before; existing SPEC/DEF artifacts without a title keep their stored epicSlug; triage callers that omit specHash get the same nextCall as today. The consolidation moves markdown only (the JSON store is untouched) and is reversible with git.

alternativesConsidered.name: One shared work-item head reader + title-first naming
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A single head reader in storage.ts (DEF -> ISSUE -> LLD) that both the tracker resolver and slug inheritance consume; heads are named from a title; triage forwards an approved specHash; the migrator's label precedence gains the LLD.
alternativesConsidered.approach: storage.ts gains one exported head reader that returns the work item's head {kind: 'DEF'|'ISSUE'|'LLD', epicSlug, anchorCreatedAt, tracker?, standalone?} by trying DEF-<h>, then ISSUE-<h>, then the lowest-ordinal LLD-<h>-<story> (any LLD, flagged or legacy). readEpicDefinitionCore and resolve.ts readEpicIdentity both delegate to it, and listEpicHashes additionally yields hashes that have an LLD but no DEF/ISSUE. Naming: a pure helper derives the label from a head title (deriveSlug(title)) and falls back to safeDeriveSlug(focus); SpecArtifactBody and DefineBody gain an optional `title` that their synthesizer schemas ask for; finalizeIssue uses its body.title; finalizeStandaloneLld uses params.storyTitle; PLAN/BUILD/TESTS/CR keep inheriting via inheritedEpicSlug, which now sees the LLD head. Triage start input gains optional specHash, verified with requireApprovedSpec, and classify forwards it into the design.story params. planMigration's label precedence becomes DEF -> ISSUE -> LLD -> other members.
pros: One definition of 'the head of a work item', so the resolver and folder naming cannot disagree again.
No new artifact kind; legacy unflagged LLDs are covered by construction.
Reuses existing seams (requireApprovedSpec, resolveStageFocus, seededFromSpec stamp, planMigration grouping).
cons: Touches two modules' readers in one change (resolve.ts + storage.ts).
SPEC/DEF schema gains a field; old artifacts without a title fall back to focus-derived names.

alternativesConsidered.name: Patch each reader independently
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add an LLD branch separately to readEpicIdentity/listEpicHashes in resolve.ts and to readEpicDefinitionCore in storage.ts, with naming and triage changes as in a1.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Each existing reader keeps its own file list and gains its own 'then try LLD-<h>-*' step; listEpicHashes adds an LLD_RE pass. Naming, triage specHash and migrator precedence change as in a1.
pros: Smallest diff per file; no new shared function.
Each reader stays readable on its own.
cons: Three places now encode the DEF -> ISSUE -> LLD order; they already drifted once (resolve.ts and storage.ts were written separately).
Story-ordinal choice for multi-LLD hashes would be duplicated.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Meets the SPEC but keeps the head order duplicated in three places.

alternativesConsidered.name: Stamp an explicit anchor flag on the LLD
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: finalizeStandaloneLld stamps meta.anchor=true; readers accept only flagged LLDs; a migration stamps legacy LLDs.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Readers look for an LLD whose meta carries an explicit anchor marker; existing standalone LLDs (and the 7 unflagged legacy ones) get the marker written by a one-off migration over .insrc/artifacts.
pros: Anchoring is explicit in the data, not inferred from absence of DEF/ISSUE.
cons: Rewrites artifact JSON for history, which the SPEC's 'any LLD, flagged or not' decision avoids.
Adds a migration step that touches approved artifacts.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates the SPEC's any-LLD decision by rewriting approved artifacts.
